🔊 USA vs. Australia World Cup 2026: Team news, lineups, and how to watch

📌 Discover the latest team news, expected lineups, and how to watch the 2026 World Cup Group D clash between the USA and Australia at Lumen Field.

It’s the biggest game of Group D so far. The United States hosts Australia at Lumen Field in Seattle on Friday, with both nations carrying perfect records into a clash that could seal qualification for the round of 32. Mauricio Pochettino’s side announced themselves to the world with a dominant 4-1 dismantling of Paraguay, while Tony Popovic’s Socceroos pulled off one of matchday one’s biggest shocks by beating Türkiye 2-0. Two wins from two would put either team in an almost unassailable position — and neither side can afford to blink.
​
This Group D showdown at Lumen Field is one of the most anticipated second-round fixtures of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Both teams arrive on three points and in confident form, making this a de facto battle for top spot in the group. German referee Felix Zwayer has been appointed to take charge.
​
Fans across the globe can tune into this crucial World Cup encounter through the following broadcasters:
​
The only real concern heading into this fixture surrounds Christian Pulisic, who was withdrawn at half-time during the Paraguay match after picking up a knock. However, both Pochettino and captain Tyler Adams have publicly confirmed that Pulisic will be available to face Australia. Barring that worry, Pochettino is expected to name an unchanged starting XI — there is little reason to tinker with a side that produced the USA’s largest winning margin in World Cup history.
​
Forward Mohamed Toure was substituted late in the win over Türkiye with cramps and some concerns around his calf muscle. Reports ahead of the game indicate he is expected to be fit and available for selection. Like Pochettino, Popovic looks set to name the same XI that started against Türkiye, with goalkeeper Patrick Beach — who made eight saves on his competitive debut — the standout performer likely to retain his place between the sticks.
​
The USMNT carries the momentum of a massive World Cup opening win, while Australia hopes to build on its massive upset.
​
The USA enters this fixture as clear favorites, and rightly so. Pochettino has built a side with genuine World Cup pedigree — Pulisic, Balogun, McKennie, Reyna, and Tillman represent an attacking unit capable of hurting any defense in the world. Their 4-1 win over Paraguay was not just a scoreline; it was a statement of intent, delivered with tempo and intensity from the first whistle.
​
Yet Australia’s win over Türkiye showed exactly why Popovic’s side should not be dismissed. They are disciplined, organized, and ruthlessly efficient on the counter. Irankunda is a genuine danger in transition, and if Beach can reproduce anything close to his performance against Türkiye, a repeat clean sheet is not out of the question. Popovic will set up his low block knowing that the USA have not kept a clean sheet in nine games — and that even a draw from this fixture would likely be enough to confirm progression to the knockout stages.
​
The biggest tactical question is whether Pochettino’s high-energy press will work against a team that is happy to absorb pressure and hit on the break. It did not work for Türkiye, and Popovic will have noted that carefully. This has all the ingredients of a game where the scoreline may not reflect how close the contest truly was.
